pageCache.pageTitle: Eco-Saints Worship - News - Netheravon All Saints Primary School
pageCache.text:
Eco-Saints Worship
Thank-you to the children in Eco-Saints for leading worship on Monday 10th February and their passionate appeal to make our school a better place for wildlife. The children hope to complete a range of projects to improve our school grounds for wildlife this spring, one of which will be the 'Great Big School Clean', a national initiative taking place on Thursday 27th March. Using a collection of litter-picking equipment provided to us by Wiltshire Council, the children will work together to clear the school's outside spaces, and they are keen to carry on their clean up outside of school too!

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values and Protected Characteristics - Netheravon All Saints Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values and Protected Characteristics
The Department for Education has published guidance to schools on promoting British values to prepare young people for life in modern Britain. This is at the heart of what we teach at Netheravon All Saints C of E Primary School. We teach and support the fundamental British values of:
We live these values as part of our everyday life at Netheravon – we have rules to keep us safe and learning. These values are embedded throughout our curriculum, our Worship and daily school life - they are central to our Personal Development offer.
At Netheravon, we choose our Collective Worship Team, House Captains and School Council. We respect each other’s views and beliefs and treat everyone equally and kindly as part of our team.
British Values are also taught explicitly through Personal, Social, Health and Emotional (PSHE), and Religious Education (RE). We also teach British Values through planning and delivering a broad and balanced curriculum.
We use the Jigsaw PSHE scheme which also specifically promotes the fundamental British values. Jigsaw contributes, as a good PSHE programme should, to the British Values agenda very significantly, both through the direct teaching of information and through the experiential learning children will enjoy.
The strands of the British Values agenda have been mapped across every Puzzle and every Piece (lesson) which you can see below.
Netheravon British Values Progression
To support curriculum delivery the school also utilises the Picture News resources, which we share in a whole class Worship once a week. These expose the children to current news stories with an inspirational image and thought-provoking questions. This helps the children of Netheravon to gain a deeper understanding of the wider world and current events that are happening, in a manner in which they understand and may otherwise have not been made aware of.
We find that using such engaging and inspiring resources ignites a passion in our children to learn more about key issues for their generation while also promoting British Values.
As well as the British Values, we are committed to Equalities Education. We work to ensure that our children understand that:
The Equality Act became law in 2010. It covers everyone in Britain and protects people from discrimination, harassment and victimisation - everyone in Britain is protected. This is because the Equality Act protects people against discrimination because of the protected characteristics that we all have. Under the Equality Act, there are nine Protected Characteristics:
At Netheravon, we teach and promote these in our curriculum and embed them into our ethos. Our vision and values, enable us to ensure children understand and show the love, acceptance and tolerance to all that we expect.
You can read about our approach to the Protected Characteristics in the document below and on our Personal Development page.
Protected Characteristics
Democracy
The rule of law
Individual liberty
Mutual respect and tolerance
Everyone is different
We celebrate our differences
We are all equal in our differences
Disability
Gender reassignment
Religion or belief
Marriage or civil partnership
Sexual orientation

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - Netheravon All Saints Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Netheravon Primary School!
We are a proud Church school, right at the heart of our community, where everyone is valued and encouraged to grow in every way—academically, spiritually, and personally. Our Christian values guide all we do, helping us to build a caring, respectful and inclusive environment where children feel safe, supported and inspired.
Netheravon All Saints Primary School is a place where our children are at the centre of everything we do: the curriculum, experiences and nurture we provide; the decisions we make; and the commitment staff and the wider community have to ensure children at our school thrive.
As a values-based school, we pride ourselves on the way in which our children grow in every sense during their time at Netheravon. Developing values such as service, courage, kindness, and cooperation allows them to become independent and responsible individuals and gives them the foundations for success.
The daily curriculum provided by the staff is supported by a range of enrichment opportunities throughout the year to develop our broad and balanced curriculum that goes beyond academic requirements.
We have an ‘open door’ policy here at Netheravon, and we are always more than happy to discuss your children with you. I am also delighted to welcome new parents for a tour of the school. If you do have any questions or queries, please contact the school office via email (admin@allsaints-netheravon.wilts.sch.uk) or via telephone (01980670339).

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values - Netheravon All Saints Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Service Courage Faith
a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; }
At our school, every child is valued, nurtured and encouraged to grow into the best version of themselves. Rooted in Christian principles, we want our pupils to flourish academically, socially and personally in a joyful, welcoming and supportive community where children feel safe, confident and excited to learn.
Our vision and ethos is underpinned by the following quote from Joshua 1:9
'Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God is always with you.'
As an inclusive, Christian school, both adults and children are valued and strong relationships are built on trust and respect. We give children the space to discover their strengths, build positive relationships and develop the character that will help them thrive in the world beyond our school.
At Netheravon, the value of service is at the heart of all we do. With many of our parents currently serving in the Armed Forces, it is also a strong value within those in our community. Children are encouraged to recognise, and show service to one another in school and the wider community.
a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; }
a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; }
In our school, all adults help children develop courage by creating a safe and supportive environment where everyone believes they can be confident to have a go, take risks and believe in themselves. Children are taught that courage isn’t only about being brave in big moments, but also about courageous advocacy, trying something new, learning from mistakes and persevering when things feel challenging. Staff encourage children to step out of their comfort zone, praising effort, resilience and determination.
a { text-decoration: none; color: #464feb; } tr th, tr td { border: 1px solid #e6e6e6; } tr th { background-color: #f5f5f5; }
We understand faith as a sense of hope, trust and belief in something bigger than ourselves. As a community, we are committed to helping children grow in faith by giving them meaningful opportunities to think, reflect and explore the values that guide them.
We work closely with all our Acorn Education Trust family of schools to enrich the primary curriculum and to create opportunities for an educationally seamless journey from 3 to 18 years of age.

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship - Netheravon All Saints Primary School
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
At Netheravon All Saints we provide religious education and daily collective worship for all registered pupils and actively promote their spiritual, moral and cultural development.
Collective worship takes place every morning, with the school community coming together at the start of the day. Worship is led by the Headteacher or another member of the teaching staff, with children sometimes leading as well. On a Thursday morning a member of the local clergy comes in to deliver worship, and on a Friday we celebrate children's achievements with certificates and other awards. Worship gives us the opportunity to sing together, listen to or join in with a prayer, and to have a quiet moment of reflection before our daily learning begins.
Each term, we focus on one of our values or an aspect of our vision statement to deepen the children's understanding of these key aspects of our school life. These are explored through stories and examples of people - past or present - who have demonstrated these values. As such, worship forms an important part of our personal development curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 4 /5 Science - News - Netheravon All Saints Primary School
pageCache.text:
Year 4 /5 Science
This term in Science, Year 4/5 have been looking at forces. In particular, we have been thinking about the forces that act when deploying parachutes. The students have thought scientifically and have shown great understanding of how a parachute can slow the load down.
As part of their learning, the students had to create a parachute that was to be attached to an egg and dropped from a height. The design was up to them, but the aim was to safely get the egg to the ground and avoid any cracks. The children worked hard, thinking about how the surface area of the parachute would affect the amount of air resistance, and in turn affect the speed. We had lots of successful experiments, as well as some super evaluations afterwards.
To finish off our unit, we were lucky enough to have a parachute donated by the Netheravon Army Parachute Association. The child were stunned by the size of the canopy and excited to open the parachute up and explore.
Well done on a super term of scientific learning.
